name: language
description: Quadrate language syntax and keywords reference

types.name: i8
types.description: 8-bit signed integer. Only valid in struct fields and mem accessors; promotes to i64 on the stack (sign-extended on load, truncated on store).

types.name: i16
types.description: 16-bit signed integer. Only valid in struct fields and mem accessors; promotes to i64 on the stack (sign-extended on load, truncated on store).

types.name: i32
types.description: 32-bit signed integer. Only valid in struct fields and mem accessors; promotes to i64 on the stack (sign-extended on load, truncated on store).

types.name: u8
types.description: 8-bit unsigned integer. Only valid in struct fields and mem accessors; promotes to i64 on the stack (zero-extended on load, truncated on store).

types.name: u16
types.description: 16-bit unsigned integer. Only valid in struct fields and mem accessors; promotes to i64 on the stack (zero-extended on load, truncated on store).

types.name: u32
types.description: 32-bit unsigned integer. Only valid in struct fields and mem accessors; promotes to i64 on the stack (zero-extended on load, truncated on store).

types.name: u64
types.description: 64-bit unsigned integer (memory width). Stack representation is i64, so values above 2^63-1 appear as negative on the stack. Prefer i64 unless the memory layout specifically requires unsigned semantics.

keywords.description: Pops a value from the stack and binds it to a local variable

keywords.name: Err
keywords.description: Error result constant. Equivalent to integer 0 (false).

keywords.name: Ok
keywords.description: Success result constant. Equivalent to integer 1 (true).
Wildcard/default case in switch statements

keywords.name: as
keywords.description: Type narrowing cast for struct field access on ptr values. Compile-time only, no runtime cost.

keywords.name: break
keywords.description: Exits the innermost loop immediately
examples: 0 100 1 for i { i found if { break } }

keywords.name: const
keywords.description: Declares a compile-time constant value

keywords.name: var
keywords.description: Declares a module-level mutable global variable. Initializer is required; the :type annotation is optional — when omitted, the type is inferred from the initializer (int→i64, float→f64, string→str, from a referenced const's value shape, or from a struct construction's type). Struct constructions run once before main. Use pub var to export.

keywords.name: continue
keywords.description: Skips to the next iteration of the innermost loop
examples: 0 10 1 for i { i 5 == if { continue } i print nl }

keywords.name: ctx
keywords.description: Creates an isolated stack context; results are appended to parent stack

keywords.name: defer
keywords.description: Schedules a block to run when the function exits, in LIFO order

keywords.name: else
keywords.description: Provides an alternative block when the if condition is false

keywords.name: enum
keywords.description: Declares scoped named integer constants. Values auto-increment from 0 or from the last explicit value.

keywords.name: type
keywords.description: Declares a type alias. The alias is resolved at compile time with no runtime cost.

keywords.name: false
keywords.description: Boolean false literal (pushes 0 onto the stack)

keywords.name: fn
keywords.description: Declares a function with a stack signature

keywords.name: for
keywords.description: Iterates from start to end with a step, binding the iterator variable
keywords.syntax: start end step for var { body }

keywords.name: if
keywords.description: Executes a block if the top of stack is true (non-zero)

keywords.name: inline
keywords.description: Requests the compiler to inline a function at call sites, eliminating function call overhead. Can be combined with pub.
examples: pub inline fn inc(x:i64 -- result:i64) { x 1 + }

keywords.name: import
keywords.description: Imports a C library, declaring its functions with Quadrate signatures
examples: import "libm.so" as "m" { pub fn sin(x:f64 -- y:f64) }
import "mylib.a" as "my" { pub fn process(data:ptr len:i64 -- result:i64) }

keywords.name: loop
keywords.description: Repeats a block indefinitely until break is called
examples: loop { input process done if { break } }
0 -> count loop { count inc -> count count 10 > if { break } }

keywords.name: null
keywords.description: Null pointer constant. Pushes 0 with pointer type. Use for empty pointer fields in structs.
examples: ptr null == if { "is null" print nl }

keywords.name: pub
keywords.description: Makes a function, constant, or struct visible to other modules

keywords.name: return
keywords.description: Exits the current function immediately
examples: fn early() { true if { return } "not reached" print }
fn find(x:i64 -- found:bool) { check if { true return } false }

keywords.name: struct
keywords.description: Declares a structured data type with named fields

keywords.name: packed
keywords.description: Struct modifier: fields laid out adjacent at exact widths with no padding. Use for parsing on-disk binary formats. Combines with pub.
examples: packed struct FileLump { offset:u32 size:u32 name:u64 }
pub packed struct PngChunk { length:u32 type:u32 }

keywords.name: switch
keywords.description: Branches based on matching the top of stack against case values
keywords.syntax: value switch { case1 { block1 } case2 { block2 } _ { default } }

keywords.name: test
keywords.description: Declares a test function. Tests are run with quadc --test or quad test.

keywords.name: true
keywords.description: Boolean true literal (pushes 1 onto the stack)

keywords.name: use
keywords.description: Imports a module, making its functions available with module::function syntax

keywords.name: while
keywords.description: Repeats a block while the condition on the stack is true
examples: 1 -> x x 10 < while { x print nl x 1 + -> x x 10 < }

operators.description: Returns 1 if a equals b, 0 otherwise
Returns 1 if a does not equal b
Returns 1 if a is less than b
Returns 1 if a is less than or equal to b
Returns 1 if a is greater than b
Returns 1 if a is greater than or equal to b
Left shift a by n bits
Right shift a by n bits

syntax_patterns.name: Function Definition
syntax_patterns.description: Parameters before -- are inputs (popped from stack), after -- are outputs (pushed to stack)
examples: fn greet(name:str --) { "Hello, " print name print nl }

syntax_patterns.name: Generic Function
syntax_patterns.description: Generic functions work with multiple types
examples: fn swap_pair<T>(a:T b:T -- b:T a:T) { swap }

syntax_patterns.name: Method Definition
syntax_patterns.description: Methods operate on a struct instance
examples: fn (self:Point) magnitude(-- m:f64) { self@x sq self@y sq + sqrt }

syntax_patterns.name: String Interpolation
syntax_patterns.description: Embed expressions in strings with curly braces

syntax_patterns.name: Array Literal
syntax_patterns.description: Creates an array with the given elements

syntax_patterns.name: Field Assignment
syntax_patterns.description: Assigns a value to a struct field

syntax_patterns.name: Module Function Call
syntax_patterns.description: Calls a function from an imported module
